analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: changelog.d/deadline-admission-estimators.md (new, lines 1-6) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (a new 'Deadline admission rates' section at head lines 523-548 and a code-map row at 602). No executable source, wire format, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption code changed in the supplied units. The Swift implementation (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift) is referenced but not supplied, so the described estimator behavior is an unverified contract.

The docs describe changes to first-token deadline admission estimators: per-batch-step decode charging, an anchor floor at 1/8 of the startup idle calibration rate, and a 30-minute staleness cutoff. They state that the changes alter no KV grant, load quotation, activation floor, serving width or memory concurrency, and that admitted requests still pass slot and process byte admission. The anchor applies only at nominal posture, with no Low Power Mode and nominal thermal state. Published rates and capacity wire fields are unchanged. This is a time-admission heuristic, not a security control. It is relevant only to availability or overcommit (T-010, T-029, T-016), and the docs say memory admission remains authoritative.

A new env var, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0, is forwarded by `darkbloom start` to the background launchd provider. This is operator-local configuration under the existing operator trust model (TB-003), and the supplied evidence does not show a way to widen privilege through it. The integration question is whether the real code could let a lowered pricing floor admit more deadline-bound requests than the provider can serve, which would be a performance or SLA issue rather than a confidentiality or integrity regression. Whether the floor and anchor logic matches the docs needs confirmation in the Swift source, which is not in this batch. No threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations are invalidated by the documentation.
